papers.title: Elementary Subgroups in Isotropic Reductive Groups

coverage.venue: Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians 2026, Volume 3: Invited Lectures (Sections 1-4), SIAM
coverage.reading: Read the complete mathematical body, Sections 1, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1 and 3.2, pp. 293-300, including proofs of Theorems 2.1 and 3.6; checked the bibliography on pp. 300-304. Official HTML and official PDF text extraction were cross-checked.
integrated_results: Theorem 3.5 (affine-group specialization of the stated KV_1 conclusion)
proof_coverage: Expanded the conjugation proof of Corollary 2.2.
Expanded the opposite-parabolic independence argument, conditional on the Levi conjugacy theorem.
Preserved the semilocal argument of Theorem 2.1(ii), explicitly depending on minimal-parabolic existence and conjugacy.
Expanded the contraction and endpoint-evaluation arguments relating K_1 and KV_1, conditional on the vector-scheme structure theorem.
Preserved the two-map proof of Theorem 3.6, conditional on A^1-invariance of torsors and affine representability.
Theorem 2.4 is accompanied only by the reported level-computation/generic-element proof route, not an invented proof.
coverage.background: Added local definitions for reductive-group torsor and K-theory prerequisites, reusing parent canonical scheme/module nodes and the concurrent Achar-Riche root-data node 0187.

deepening.summary: Historical first-pass coverage above is preserved. Added fully written split-matrix proofs for commutators, semilocal SL=E and normality, Jacobson-level relative SL=E and commutators, stable Whitehead, determinant K1/stabilization and reduction maps, plus explicit polynomial paths and rank/normal-closure/lifting counterexamples.
deepening.generalization_boundary: No claim to complete the general relative-root/local-global/A1-torsor proofs or arbitrary stable-range theory.

limitations: Direct download of the official PDF binary to /tmp was attempted through /doi/pdf and /doi/epdf, including an approved unsandboxed attempt; every curl request returned HTTP 403. The actual official full text was nevertheless read through the web tool, which extracted the 12-page PDF, and via the publisher's full HTML. No local PDF binary or successful pdftotext run is claimed.
No arXiv version of this exact ICM2026 report was located; older Stavrova papers were not substituted.

Reading a survey statement is not reading the proofs in its bibliography. The proofs of the root calculations, local-global principle, sandwich classification, affine Horrocks theorem, injectivity, Henselian rigidity, polynomial invariance, torsor invariance and affine representability are not exhaustively reproduced or independently verified.

First-pass limitation (historical): relative root subschemes, general Weil restriction, LG-rings, stabilization, congruence kernels and higher Karoubi-Villamayor groups were not developed into complete prerequisite networks. Current deepening resolves the concrete split matrix commutator, semilocal/Jacobson congruence, stable Whitehead and explicitly bounded K1 branches recorded in deepening; all general/non-split and higher-degree gaps remain.
The Kneser-Tits/abelianity question is recorded with the status given by the report, not a claim that all later literature up to the run date was exhaustively surveyed.
The source's parenthetical identification of groups without proper parabolics with tori is not adopted: anisotropic semisimple groups provide another possibility.
The contraction paragraph's h(X)=g endpoint typo is corrected to h(1)=g; Theorem 3.5's unused quantified n is not converted into an unsupported higher-degree theorem.
Shared foundations and root navigation remain the parent's responsibility. Only allocated files were edited; no whole-site build, root audit or navigation update was performed.

01Q0.reason: Navigation only. Orders all 28 new mathematical nodes and one supporting reference; explicitly separates concrete proofs from general reductive local-global and torsor results.

01Q1.reason: Extends the existing field-only GL definition 00DD to commutative rings without redefining rings/modules; defines SL and decodes determinant, adjugate, units and matrix multiplication locally.

01Q2.reason: Canonical elementary-matrix definition extracted from the older parabolic example 01EB, whose terminology now directly links here; includes inverse, determinant, row/column and functorial conventions.

01Q3.reason: Checked every index case by matrix-unit multiplication, including the negative sign and the excluded opposite-root case; complete proof in the node.

01Q4.reason: Complete perfectness proof with an explicit third index; matrix size n>=3 distinguished from semisimple rank n-1.

01Q5.reason: Six-element computation and faithful action on the three nonzero F2-vectors prove E2=SL2=S3 and nonperfectness; does not falsely claim nonnormality.

01Q6.reason: Six-factor unit diagonal formula checked by two-stage multiplication; all coordinate indices and invertibility hypotheses introduced.

01Q7.reason: Defines unimodularity through the already canonical generated ideal 00GB and explains inverse-row coefficients; no duplicate module definition.

01Q8.reason: Complete finite residue-field coefficient gluing, including explicit separating elements for pairwise comaximal maximal ideals and the unit test; not a polynomial local-global proof.

01Q9.reason: Precise finite-rank semilocal SL=E statement, with standalone proof 01QA; does not claim the prescribed four-factor general Gauss decomposition.

01QA.reason: Assumptions and target theorem restated. Unit pivot, left/right clearing, paired unit normalization and the n=2 terminal case all checked.

01QB.reason: Normality proved from the determinant kernel after SL=E, not assumed to form the quotient; injectivity and surjectivity of the determinant quotient both proved.

01QC.reason: New canonical Jacobson-radical definition, reusing maximal ideals and local rings; distinguishes containment in J(R) from a radical ideal in the commutative-algebra sense.

01QD.reason: Both directions of the maximal-ideal unit criterion, subgroup property of 1+I and lifting quotient units are proved explicitly; no Hensel input.

01QE.reason: Compares the six factors in E_n/E_n(R,I), whose denominator is normal by definition; does not assume the relative reduction-kernel equality it will help prove.

01QF.reason: Exact assumptions I subset J(R), n>=2, arbitrary commutative R; links standalone proof 01QG and derives ambient GL normality from two kernels.

01QG.reason: Assumptions and theorem restated; every clearing coefficient stays in I and the diagonal step uses 01QE. No circular quotient argument or external commutator theorem.

01QH.reason: Mod-four invariant of the subgroup generated without normal closure and an explicit conjugated 2x2 matrix prove strict containment.

01QI.reason: Complete Jacobson-level relative commutator proof via determinant/reduction kernels and the third-index identity; arbitrary-ideal general reductive theorem remains external.

01QJ.reason: Stable groups defined as eventual-identity matrices with finite-size representatives, explicitly distinguishing stable E(R) from fixed reductive-group notation.

01QK.reason: All off-diagonal blocks factored into ordinary elementary matrices, then six block factors multiplied; no unproved block-to-elementary step.

01QL.reason: Stable Whitehead equality stated with finite-size meaning; separate complete proof 01QM. No unsupported finite-rank stability conclusion.

01QM.reason: Assumptions and target theorem restated; both subgroup inclusions proved by a third index and a verified three-diagonal-block identity.

01QN.reason: Stable K1 is a group by Whitehead; finite-rank quotients remain pointed sets until normality is established; comparison maps are justified on representatives.

01QO.reason: Both finite and stable semilocal quotients computed by determinant; explicit n>=2 scope and optional trivial n=1 convention avoid claiming a sharp bound.

01QP.reason: Relative finite and stable quotients computed as 1+I using the proved relative kernel equality; R need not be semilocal and arbitrary ideals are excluded.

01QQ.reason: Exactness proved by identifying all three maps with units, inclusion and quotient reduction; quotient semilocality and unit surjectivity justified.

01QR.reason: Absolute and relative paths given as finite products, including conjugators and ideal parameters; no inverse of a polynomial interpolation is assumed and no torsor/A1-representability claim made.

01QS.reason: Supporting primary-author exposition, not a replacement for the exact Stavrova report; read scope and terminology restriction recorded.

01QT.reason: Generator lifting proves E-surjectivity only; mod-five determinant gives a complete GL-surjectivity counterexample in every size.
